title: Quantization Failure Modes and Recovery Playbook
author: Leah Martinez
body:
Overview:

This playbook documents known failure modes introduced or exposed by quantization during model onboarding and serving, detection signals, prioritized triage steps, short-term mitigations, and long-term remediation patterns. It is intended for ML engineers, inference runtime owners, and SREs who operate Redwood's model-serving stacks across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope:

- Applies to transformer family models served on CPU and GPU inference stacks when using 8-bit and 4-bit quantization profiles (symmetric/asymmetric, PTQ/QAT variations).
- Covers failures observable at inference time (latency, correctness, stability) and offline evaluation regressions discovered during continuous evals.
- Excludes model training or pre-training data issues (those are covered in model-onboarding onboarding docs).

Failure mode taxonomy (highest priority first):

1) Semantic regression (output degradation)
- Symptom: measurable drop in task-level eval metrics (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/F1, classification accuracy) or user-reported quality regressions.
- Root causes: quantization-induced weight rounding, per-channel scale mismatch, attention head saturation, or mixed-precision KV cache inconsistency.

2) Numeric instability / hallucination spikes
- Symptom: sudden increase in nonsensical outputs or repeated tokens; elevated perplexity and token-loss signals.
- Root causes: saturation in softmax computation, reduced dynamic range causing logit collapse, accumulation error across layers.

3) KV cache corruption / context degradation
- Symptom: degraded continuation quality when using long-context; incorrect references to earlier context; cache mismatch between quantized and full-precision code paths.
- Root causes: differing rounding between KV cache write/read, truncated keys/values due to scale clipping.

4) Latency regressions under load
- Symptom: 20%+ tail-latency increases observed in p95/p99 when batching or serving longer sequences.
- Root causes: fallback to slower kernels for numerical safety, increased memory bandwidth contention with quantized kernels, or unexpected TensorRT/cuBLAS kernel selection.

5) Serialization / compatibility errors in model artifacts
- Symptom: model fails to load or runtime throws shape/dtype mismatches during deploy.
- Root causes: mismatched exporter quant config, version skew between compile toolchain and runtime.

Detection signals and dashboards to check:

- Continuous eval delta: daily eval job showing task metric drop >= 1.5x standard deviation over baseline.
- Token-level logit drift: mean logit magnitude change > 10% on held-out prompts.
- Embedding cosine drift: reduction > 0.02 from baseline for representative embedding set.
- Inference SLO metrics: p95/p99 latency increase > 15% compared to model baseline on same hardware.
- Error logs: kernel-fallback traces, dtype-conversion warnings, KV checksum mismatches.
- Customer-facing signals: increase in support tickets with "nonsense" or "context loss" tags, and automated quality-alert annotations.

Quick triage checklist (first 30–90 minutes):

1) Verify rollout and config
- Confirm the quantized model variant that rolled out (model id, quant profile id, compile toolchain).
- Check rollout policy: canary percentage, pinned tenants, and automatic fallback settings.

2) Reproduce locally against golden prompts
- Use the eval harness to run the failing prompt set at exact generation parameters (temperature, top-k, max_tokens).
- Compare outputs between float32 baseline and quantized candidate.

3) Check telemetry and logs
- Inspect evaluation diffs: metric deltas, per-prompt failure histogram.
- Search runtime logs for kernel fallback, dtype warnings, or cache checksum mismatches.

4) Determine scope (global vs workload-specific)
- Run the failing prompts across multiple tenants/instances to see if issue is universal or context-dependent.

Immediate mitigations (order of preference):

- Automatic fallback: trigger a rollback to the last-known-good float32 or higher-precision variant for affected tenants via the rollout API.
- Canary expansion pause: stop canary expansion and set quantized variant to 0% traffic.
- Per-route override: pin high-risk routes to full-precision model until remediation complete.
- Temporary scheduler change: reduce batch size or disable batching heuristic that increases sequence lengths if latency is the issue.

Runbook: step-by-step escalation (detailed)

1) Level 1 (on-call ML engineer)
- Action: gather minimal reproducible example and run local A/B: float32 vs quantized.
- Commands (examples):

  # Run eval harness on source-of-truth prompts
  rdinfer-eval --model-id rdm/my-model:1.2.0 --variant quant-q4_8 --prompt-file failing_prompts.jsonl --seed 42 --out diffs.json

  # Compare embeddings
  rdinfer-embed-diff --baseline rdm/my-model:1.2.0-fp32 --candidate rdm/my-model:1.2.0-quantq4 --set small_embedding_suite.jsonl --metrics cosine,mag

- Output to capture: eval deltas, example mismatches, stderr from runtime.

2) Level 2 (runtime or quantization SME)
- Action: inspect kernel selection and numerical diagnostics on affected nodes.
- Commands / checks:
  - Check kernel trace logs for fallback paths (grep runtime.log "fallback" or "kernel_mismatch").
  - Run deterministic single-threaded inference with debug numerics enabled: rdinfer-run --debug-numerics=trace --model <candidate> --prompt "<example>"

- If KV cache corruption suspected: dump KV vectors from both candidate and baseline and compute element-wise differences.

3) Level 3 (release/engineering leads)
- Action: authorize rollback if automatic mitigations did not restore safety. Coordinate customer comms and incident tracking.

Root-cause remediation patterns (long term):

- Per-layer calibration: introduce per-channel min/max calibration and compare with per-layer symmetric vs asymmetric scales.
- Mixed-precision policy: for sensitive attention/softmax layers, mark as FP16/FP32 during compilation.
- KV cache consistency tests: add unit tests that assert round-trip equality for cached keys/values across quantized and unquantized code paths (tolerance thresholds).
- Kernel selection whitelist: maintain a registry of vetted kernels per model family/sequence-length profile to avoid performance fallbacks.
- Incremental rollout policies: stronger offline gating (staged eval with production-like prompts) before canary traffic.

Testing and CI additions (must-haves):

- Add a nightly quant-smoke job that runs a fixed suite of 5k prompts across representative workloads, capturing metric deltas, logit distributions, and KV checksum.
- Add a synthetic adversarial prompt set that attempts to amplify quantization numerical issues (long token repetition, extreme logits, edge-case tokenization).
- Integrate embedding drift alerting into primary observability pipeline with automatic ticket creation when thresholds exceeded.

Telemetry and alerting recommendations:

- New alert: QUANT_EVAL_DEGRADE when model-variant daily eval score delta > 2% and at least 50 failing prompts. Severity: P2.
- New metric: kv_checksum_mismatch_rate per model-variant (increase triggers P3).
- Dashboard panels to include: per-prompt delta waterfall, kernel-fallback timeline, p95/p99 latency by variant, logit-magnitude distributions.

Ownership and escalation contacts:

- Primary owner: Applied ML — model-serving squad (team-email: applied-ml@redwood.com).
- Runtime SME: eng-serving-runtime kernel team (kernel-sme@redwood.com).
- On-call SRE contact: eng-sre rotation (see oncall roster).

Post-incident: retrospective checklist

- Annotate eval dataset with failing prompts and classification of failure mode.
- Create a ticket for permanent remediation and attach experimental artifacts (calibration tables, kernel traces).
- Update quantization profile docs to reflect tuned thresholds or forbidden layer quantization.
- Schedule a knowledge-share session with platform and SRE teams.

Appendix A — Example config table (quant profile manifest snippet):

| field | example | description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| profile_id | q4_8_symmetric_v2 | canonical profile name |
| per_channel | true | enable per-channel scales for linear layers |
| excluded_layers | "attn.out_proj, lm_head" | comma-separated layer regex to keep at FP16 |
| calibration_method | percentile_99.9 | how activations were calibrated |
| runtime_flags | "force_kernel=v2,kv_safe_mode=true" | runtime compilation toggles |

Appendix B — Useful commands and examples:

- Export model with quant manifest:

  rdinfer-export --model src:my-model:1.2.0 --quant-profile q4_8_symmetric_v2 --out /tmp/my-model-quant.tar.gz

- Trigger immediate rollback for a model variant (admin API):

  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/admin/rollouts/rollback -d '{"model_id":"rdm/my-model:1.2.0","variant":"quant-q4_8","reason":"regression-detected"}'

Appendix C — Example reproducibility prompt (JSONL) and diffing guidance:

- Provide 50 representative prompts covering classification, summarization, long-context continuation, and code. Each prompt should include deterministic generation params (temperature 0, top_p 1.0, seed fixed).

- Diffing guidance: report per-prompt metric delta, top-3 token differences with logit delta, and human-annotated severity bucket (minor/medium/critical).

Document maintenance:

- Owner must review this playbook quarterly and after any major quantization release (toolchain, compiler, or runtime changes).
- Significant incidents must be linked here and summarized in the related_pages field.

Notes and references:

- See related internal docs: per-workload-quant-tuner-and-safety-guidelines-2026 for calibration guidance, model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026 for broader regression triage patterns.

End of document.
